draft.title: The federal Budget
card: The federal Budget is a yearly plan. It sets out how much the Australian Government expects to spend and how much revenue it expects to collect over the coming year.
Revenue is the money the government collects, mostly from taxes. Spending is what it pays out, such as on health, schools, roads and payments to people.
the government spends more than it collects in revenue. It has to borrow to cover the gap.
the government spends less than it collects in revenue. It has money left over.
draft.remember: A Budget plans spending and revenue. Spend more than you collect is a deficit, less is a surplus.

a.q: In one year the government collects $500 billion and spends $520 billion. What is this?
a.why: Spending is higher than revenue, so the Budget is in deficit. The gap is $520 billion minus $500 billion, which is $20 billion. It is not a surplus, because a surplus needs revenue to be higher than spending.
a.clue: Compare what comes in with what goes out.

b.q: A news report says the government plans to spend less next year than it expects to collect in taxes and other revenue. What does this describe?
b.why: Planned spending below expected revenue is a surplus. A deficit is the opposite, with spending above revenue. The report does not say taxes will rise, as revenue can be higher than spending at the current tax levels.
b.clue: Which is bigger, spending or revenue?
